title: Parenting the Preschooler
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: Deepening Scripture Instruction
subpoints: Preschoolers (ages 4-5) can understand deeper theological concepts than toddlers.
Children possess a natural, uncynical faith that allows them to embrace big biblical truths.
Parents should continue daily devotions and teaching, increasing depth as the child matures.

outline.title: Modeling and Discipline
subpoints: Modeling appropriate responses to commands is crucial for preschoolers.
Parents should coach children to restate instructions with the correct tone and attitude.
Spanking may be appropriate for disobedience, but must be followed by re-teaching the original instruction.

outline.title: Parental Gatekeeping of Media
subpoints: Parents are the primary filter for what children see and hear.
Ratings do not guarantee appropriateness; parents must exercise discernment.
Accountability for a child's exposure rests solely with the parents.

outline.title: The Preeminence of Christ in Education
subpoints: A Christian philosophy of education places Christ at the center of all learning.
All things are of, through, and to Christ, including the educational process.
Christ is the head of all things, not just the church, and must have preeminence in every area of life.

outline.title: The Command to Teach Diligently
subpoints: Deuteronomy 6 commands parents to teach God's Word diligently to their children.
Instruction should permeate all daily activities: sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up.
Parents are ultimately responsible for the spiritual and intellectual formation of their children.

summary:
This sermon, the fourth in the 'The Faithful Parent' series, focuses on parenting children in the preschool years (ages four and five). The speaker emphasizes that while the foundational principles of parenting remain consistent, the depth of instruction can increase as preschoolers demonstrate a greater capacity to understand biblical concepts. Parents are encouraged to leverage the natural, uncynical faith of young children to teach them the big truths of the Gospel, continuing the practice of daily devotions and scripture memorization established in earlier years.

A significant portion of the message addresses discipline and modeling. Parents are urged to actively coach their children in how to respond to commands with grace and obedience, using repetition and demonstration. When discipline such as spanking is deemed necessary, it must be followed by a re-teaching of the original instruction to ensure the child understands the expected behavior. Additionally, the sermon highlights the critical role of parents as gatekeepers of media, warning that ratings are not a substitute for parental discernment and accountability.

The latter half of the sermon transitions into a theological foundation for education, arguing that a true Christian philosophy of education must place Christ at the center of all learning. Citing passages from Romans, 1 Corinthians, Ephesians, and Colossians, the speaker asserts that Christ is the head of all things and that all activities, including education, are to be done for His glory. This leads to a discussion of Deuteronomy 6, where parents are reminded of their divine mandate to teach God's Word diligently and pervasively in their children's lives, ensuring that the fear of the Lord permeates every aspect of their upbringing.
